title: Multi-sleeve re-measure
hypothesis: Adding pairs and PEAD sleeves to the S&P engine lifts the combined book.
question: After freezing the engine, did pairs trading and post-earnings drift add independent return to the S&P book?
prior: Pairs (Gatev et al. 2006) and PEAD (Bernard and Thomas 1989) are long-documented anomalies.
citations: Gatev, E., Goetzmann, W. & Rouwenhorst, K. G. (2006). Pairs Trading. RFS 19(3).
Bernard, V. & Thomas, J. (1989). Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift. JAR 27.
method: PIT S&P 500 universe, MOO T+1, 7 bps.
Each sleeve backtested on its own, then blended.
verdict_reason: Voided by bugs we found in our own simulator. Short positions were marked as 2×entry − price (a phantom gain on every short), and short-sale proceeds were counted as buying power, so leverage spiralled. The first-run pairs result (+0.749 Sharpe, +199%) and PEAD result (+0.450) were artifacts. We do not show the v26 numbers.
lessons: Shorts are liabilities: mark them at −shares × price, never 2 × entry − price.
Size from equity, never from cash that includes short proceeds.
Pairs must open both legs or neither.

rows: phantom gain on every open short
Short proceeds counted as buying power

footer: Research code is private; methods summarised below.
